Site Index Models

Source: vignettes/articles/Site-Index-Models.qmd

Site index models included in the package

Models are grouped by function, with separate subsections for registered variants. Curve labels give the site-index levels used with each variant. Additional predictors and illustrative scenarios are stated where required; they are not defaults supplied by the model functions.

si_huang2026()

  • Function reference: si_huang2026()

Non-climate

  • Model ID: huang2026
  • Description: Huang et al. (2026) non-climate height-age model for eight Alberta species (height index at 50 years total age)
  • Reference: Huang et al. (2026)
  • Age type: Total age
  • Coverage: AB
  • Species coverage: ABIE.BAL, PICE.GLA, PICE.MAR, PINU.BAN, PINU.CON, POPU.BAL, POPU.TRE, PSEU.MEN

The default, separately fitted non-climate model uses height index at 50 years total age. Heights describe dominant/codominant trees, not a standardized plot mean of the largest-DBH stems. Ages above 180 years warn about extrapolation; ambiguous inversions are rejected.

Climate-sensitive

  • Model ID: huang2026_climate
  • Description: Huang et al. (2026) climate height-age model for eight Alberta species (inherent HI; requires species-specific previous-years MAP and MWMT averages and location-specific 1961-1990 MAP_normal and MWMT_normal)
  • Reference: Huang et al. (2026)
  • Age type: Total age
  • Coverage: AB
  • Species coverage: ABIE.BAL, PICE.GLA, PICE.MAR, PINU.BAN, PINU.CON, POPU.BAL, POPU.TRE, PSEU.MEN

Climate inputs are explicit, pre-aggregated values. MAP (mm) and MWMT (degrees C; not mean annual temperature) exclude the current year: use the previous 20 years for aspen, white spruce, balsam poplar and balsam fir; 10 years for black spruce; and all previous years since initiation for lodgepole pine, Douglas-fir and jack pine. For young trees, use only previous years since initiation, without silently omitting missing history. MAP_normal and MWMT_normal are location-specific 1961-1990 normals, kept fixed between scenarios.

Curve labels are inherent HI, so realized height at age 50 is C * HI. Equal HI does not mean equal realized height across scenarios. The climate fit at C = 1 differs from the separately fitted non-climate model. These dominant/codominant-height curves evaluate fixed-climate points, not changing-climate annual trajectories; continuous projection would require re-anchoring HI at each step and is not implemented here.

The illustrative normals below are the species-specific reference values used in Tables A33-A40 of the report, not provincial defaults. The second scenario has 10% lower MAP and 1 degree C higher MWMT, with normals unchanged. Neither scenario represents an observed site or a forecast.

species MAP_normal MWMT_normal
POPU.TRE 500 15.5
PICE.GLA 500 15.0
PINU.CON 625 14.0
PICE.MAR 550 15.0
POPU.BAL 550 15.0
ABIE.BAL 625 14.0
PSEU.MEN 625 14.5
PINU.BAN 450 16.5

For example, the aspen point predictions in Section 4.1 use:

si_huang2026(
  age = c(20, 50, 80), si = 16, species = "POPU.TRE",
  MAP = 400, MWMT = 18, MAP_normal = 500, MWMT_normal = 15.5,
  variant = "climate"
)
Climate averages equal the reference normals

Warmer/drier: MAP 10% lower, MWMT 1 degree C higher
